why: #390. `t.format()` and `t.render()` on a `Topic` that declares neither, where an import happens to share each called member's simple name — `format` an ordinary top-level function, `render` a class, and neither an extension of `Topic`. `_resolve_navigated` used to offer any import whose simple name matched the member as a candidate with no check that it was even a function, let alone an extension of the receiver, so both resolved as grounded, first-party `CALLS` edges onto the wrong kind of node entirely. A repo-wide extension table (receiver type -> extension id) built in pass 1 is what `_settle_calls` now checks the import against, instead of matching on name alone.

refusals.why: PREDICTED BEFORE SCORING (#390). `t.format()` on a `Topic` with no `format` member; `app.util.format` is imported under that name, but it is an ordinary top-level function, not an extension of `Topic`. Resolving onto it would be a name-only match with no evidence the import applies to this receiver.

excluded: A member outranks an extension in Kotlin, so `t.format()` and `t.render()` resolve to `Topic`'s own declarations and the two same-named imports are not candidates at all. That is what makes the refusals below falsifiable rather than vacuous: there is a correct answer here, and it is not the import.
